title: Applied ML Evals Field Guide: Eval Harness, Onboarding, Prompts, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's standard practices for applied ML evaluations: the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checks, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. It is intended as a day-to-day reference for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners responsible for model releases, quality monitoring, and cost/performance trade-offs.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single, actionable guide that reduces onboarding friction and standardizes regression detection and response across teams.
- Scope: Covers pre-release onboarding, continuous evaluation (offline & online), quantization validation, and the first 48 hours of regression triage. Does not replace incident postmortems or security/compliance evidence procedures.

Key components (quick map):
1) Eval harness: integration tests, CI, thresholding, SDK hooks.
2) Prompt sets & benchmarks: canonical prompt catalogs and synthetic benchmark suites.
3) Model onboarding guide: checklist and gating criteria for model variants and versions.
4) Quality guardrails: automated checks, human review flows, and monitoring signals.
5) Quantization profiles: target bitwidths, accuracy tolerance, and performance counters.
6) Regression triage playbook: detection, impact assessment, mitigation, and rollback.

Roles and ownership:
- Applied ML (owner): maintains eval harness, prompt catalog, and triage playbooks.
- Serving Runtime (support): provides perf and latency baselines, kernel tests, and capacity signals.
- Platform/Observability (support): ensures dashboards, traces, and alerting hooks are available for new models.
- Solutions / Customer Success (optional): supplies customer prompt sets where required under NDA.

Standards and acceptance criteria (high level):
See table: minimum acceptance criteria for model onboarding.

| Category | Minimum criteria | Gate | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Functional quality | Pass eval harness test-suite (>= target accuracy) | Hard | Applied ML |
| Prompt robustness | No catastrophic failures on canonical prompts (0 failures in sample of 500) | Hard | Applied ML |
| Latency | P50 <= target_latency_ms, P95 <= target_latency_ms * 2 | Soft | Serving Runtime |
| Token cost | <= baseline_cost * 1.15 for same workload | Soft | Finance/Applied ML |
| Quantized accuracy | Topline metric delta <= 1.5% vs float32 | Hard | Applied ML |
| Safety / Toxicity | No regression on safety evals (detailed thresholds in safety playbook) | Hard | Security/Applied ML |

Pre-release model onboarding procedure (step-by-step):
1. Create onboarding ticket in JIRA with model identifier (model-name:version) and target use-cases.
2. Add the model to eval harness CI (see eval-harness/README and .eval-config.yml).
3. Run baseline benchmark:
   - Offline unit tests (functional tests for tokens & tool calling).
   - Prompt-set sweep: run canonical prompts (N=500) and capture metrics.
   - Performance sweep: measure latency at target QPS and batch sizes on the reference hardware.
4. Validate quantization profile if applicable (see Quantization validation).
5. Produce onboarding report (template below) and request review from reviewers.
6. Gate: models with any "Hard" failures must not proceed to canary.

Onboarding report template (short):
- Model id: "model-name:version"
- Use-cases tested: enumerated list
- Key metrics: accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE (where applicable), P50/P95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, quantized delta%
- Known limitations and guardrails configured
- Rollout plan (canary %, fallback policy)
- Owner and reviewers with sign-off status

Eval harness implementation notes:
- Harness is a pytest-compatible suite executed in CI and on eval-hosts. Tests are stored under /evals/tests/.
- Important directories: 
  - prompt-sets/: canonical human prompts and synthetic scalars.
  - benchmarks/: automated benchmark jobs and segmentation masks.
  - profiles/: quantization performance microbenchmarks.
- CI triggers: pull-request -> lightweight tests; nightly -> full sweep across prompt sets and quantization variants.
- Example CI job snippet for GitHub Actions:

name: Evals full sweep
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  full-sweep:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Run eval harness
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pytest evals/tests --maxfail=1 -q

Prompt sets and benchmarks guidance:
- Maintain a canonical prompt catalog organized by vertical and task: {summarization, code, instruction-following, retrieval-augmented}.
- Each prompt set includes: intent, expected outputs/examples, pass/fail heuristics, and scoring scripts.
- Benchmarks include: latency-sensitive microbenchmarks, long-context tests (16k+ tokens), and safety/robustness suites.
- Version prompt sets whenever a change to scoring or selection criteria occurs; keep changelog in the prompt-sets/ directory.

Quality guardrails (automated + manual):
- Automated: threshold alerts for offline eval regressions, daily drift signals, production Canary mismatch rate > 5%.
- Manual: scheduled human reviews for semantic drift (monthly for high-impact models).
- Degradation buckets: minor (metric delta < 1%), moderate (1-5%), severe (>5% or safety failure). Each bucket defines response times in the regression triage section.

Quantization profiles and validation:
- Profiles: per-model profile describing target bitwidth (e.g., int8, int4), calibration dataset, and allowed accuracy delta.
- Validation steps:
  1) Run microbenchmarks on reference hardware and capture perf counters (throughput, GPU SM utilization, memory footprint).
  2) Run functional equivalence tests on the canonical prompts (N>=200).
  3) Compute topline delta for primary metrics; compare to allowed delta in profile.
  4) If delta exceeds threshold, iterate on calibration or fallback to higher precision.
- Example profile snippet (human readable):

Calibration dataset: eval/quantization/calibration-5k.jsonl
Target bitwidth: int8
Allowed accuracy delta: 1.5%
Fallback path: float16

Regression detection and alerting (prod):
- Signals to monitor: offline eval score changes, A/B canary mismatch rates, per-route user-reported failures, increased token counts for same intents, increase in safety/abuse signals.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Automated eval regression alert: absolute delta > 2% on primary metric over 24h.
  - Canary mismatch rate: > 5% over 1h.
  - Latency SLO breach: P95 > SLO * 2 for 5 consecutive minutes.

Regression triage playbook (first 48 hours):
1) Triage and confirm (0-30m):
   - Owner on-call (applied-ml) acknowledges alert, gathers available artifacts (eval diffs, example requests, traces).
   - Determine scope (single route, model version, region, or global).
2) Impact assessment (30-90m):
   - Quantify affected traffic %, estimate user impact, surface top 10 failing prompts/examples.
   - Check related infra signals (GPU errors, memory pressure, kernel fallback).
3) Mitigation (1-4h):
   - Hotfix options: enable model fallback (route to previous stable), increase canary health checks, reduce canary % to 0%.
   - If regression is limited to quantized variant, switch affected routes to float/half precision.
4) Root cause and rollback (4-24h):
   - If root cause is model degradation (e.g., unexpected behavior from new weights), rollback to previous version and schedule deeper investigation.
   - If root cause is inference engine/quantization bug, coordinate with eng-serving-runtime and open an incident ticket.
5) Postmortem and lessons (24-48h +):
   - Produce a short incident summary including regression vectors, fixes applied, and required follow-ups (tests to add, new prompt cases).

Communication and runbook links:
- Use #applied-ml-alerts for initial coordination and #platform-ops for runtime issues.
- Publish canary status and mitigation steps to the onboarding ticket.
- Required artifacts for postmortem: eval diff, 20 representative failing requests, CI job logs, quantization calibration artifacts.

Appendix: useful CLI and examples
- Run a prompt sweep locally (example):
  python evals/runner.py --model model-name:version --prompts prompt-sets/summarization/short-100.jsonl --output out.jsonl

- Quick check for quantized delta (example script):
python tools/quantize_check.py --float out/float_results.jsonl --quant out/quant_results.jsonl --metric accuracy --threshold 1.5

- Minimal checklist before canary:
  - [x] CI evals green
  - [x] Quantization validation (if used)
  - [x] Canary configuration (health checks, fallback)
  - [x] Observability dashboard updated
